skill.name: building-nextjs-apps
skill.description: Build and upgrade Next.js 16 App Router applications using current routing, caching, proxy, data-fetching, datetime, and interface design patterns. Use for React projects, not backend-only or non-React applications.
skill.summary: Build reliable Next.js 16 applications with current App Router and migration patterns.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, documented fetch calls, configuration access, and benign route parameters. Two unpinned npx command ranges create medium supply-chain risk. Semantic review also found a high-severity example that returns an HttpOnly session token in a response header.

remediation.issue: The proxy example exposes a session token through x-user-token.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the token server-side. Remove the response header and pass only non-sensitive, verified identity data where required.

remediation.issue: Setup instructions execute packages tagged @latest through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions and request user confirmation before installation or MCP registration.

semantic_findings.title: HttpOnly session token exposed in response header
semantic_findings.description: The proxy example copies the session cookie value into the x-user-token response header. This exposes the HttpOnly token to clients and defeats its confidentiality protection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly reads the session cookie and sets its value on a NextResponse header. The documented behavior is explicit and reproducible.

content.value_statement: Next.js 16 changes can break routes, caching, and request handling. This skill provides focused patterns for building and upgrading App Router applications.
actual_capabilities: Applies asynchronous params and searchParams patterns to pages, layouts, route handlers, and metadata.
Guides migrations from middleware to proxy and updates Turbopack, cache components, images, and parallel routes.
Structures App Router projects with layouts, API routes, server actions, and dynamic routes.
Explains server and client data fetching with fetch and SWR examples.
Converts browser datetime-local values to UTC and back for display.
Provides interface design guidance and Next.js DevTools MCP usage examples.
limitations: Targets Next.js 16 and may not match older framework behavior.
Provides guidance and examples, not a complete reusable project template.
Authentication, validation, and authorization examples require project-specific hardening.
DevTools MCP setup depends on an external package and a running development server.

use_cases.title: Start a Next.js application
use_cases.description: Create an App Router structure with current routing, data fetching, and interface patterns.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers starting new React applications

use_cases.title: Upgrade to Next.js 16
use_cases.description: Identify breaking changes and update routes, proxy behavior, caching, images, and Turbopack configuration.

use_cases.title: Build full-stack application flows
use_cases.description: Design server actions, API routes, authenticated backend requests, and timezone-aware forms.
use_cases.target_user: Full-stack developers using the App Router

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Next.js 16 App Router page for [feature]. Use TypeScript and explain the file location.

prompt_templates.title: Add a dynamic route
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Next.js 16 dynamic route for [resource]. Handle asynchronous params, loading, missing data, and metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Upgrade an existing project
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js 15 project for version 16 changes. Update routing, proxy, caching, images, and Turbopack while preserving behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design an authenticated data flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Next.js 16 authenticated data flow for [workflow]. Include server boundaries, validation, authorization, token protection, error states, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Create a dynamic product page with metadata and a missing-product state.
output: A route plan using an asynchronous product identifier.

output_examples.input: Upgrade a dashboard from Next.js 15 to Next.js 16.
output: A migration checklist covering proxy, asynchronous route values, caching, images, and Turbopack.
A list of affected files and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Add a local due-date field that stores UTC.
output: UTC storage guidance and local display behavior.
Validation cases for empty, invalid, and daylight-saving values.

best_practices: Confirm the installed Next.js version before applying version-specific patterns.
Keep secrets and session tokens on the server, and validate every external input.
Test migrations with type checks, builds, route navigation, and runtime diagnostics.
anti_patterns: Do not treat params or searchParams as synchronous values in Next.js 16.
Do not expose session tokens through client-visible headers or public environment variables.
Do not execute unpinned registry packages without reviewing the package and requesting confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill support the Pages Router?
faq.answer: Its primary guidance targets the Next.js 16 App Router. Pages Router projects need separate patterns.

faq.question: Can it upgrade a Next.js 15 project?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers major version 16 changes, but you must test project-specific dependencies and behavior.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete application?
faq.answer: It guides application design and implementation. The final scope depends on your requirements and existing repository.

faq.question: Does it include authentication?
faq.answer: It includes proxy and cookie examples. Production authentication still requires validated sessions, authorization, CSRF protection, and secure token handling.

faq.question: Can it handle timezones?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains converting datetime-local input to UTC and displaying stored UTC values in local time.

faq.question: Is Next.js DevTools MCP required?
faq.answer: No. It is optional for documentation, diagnostics, browser testing, and migration assistance.
